levelRule: Level-based games need at least 20 authored levels with level select through env.progress.

records.hashCheck: The reviewer recorded the hashes at the start and the end of each round; they were unchanged.

findings.observation: The move prompt gave the Manhattan distance to the target while the arrow named only one leg, so a follower pressing the arrow exactly N times overshot and stalled on 16 of 22 rooms. The number is now the length of the leg along the arrow; a batch-literal follower clears every room.

Rooms had 2 to 12 switches, several inert, and an informed random turner won 16 to 40 of 40 on most rooms 3-15. Rooms 6-22 were rebuilt with 9-12 live switches and exactly one solved setting each, with budgets of optimal +1 or +2 on eight rooms. Informed random now wins at most 5 of 40 from room 6, a beam-aware greedy at most 12 of 60 at 300 s and none of rooms 16-22, and random walk with undo at most 10 of 40 at 300 s. Rooms 1-5 are recorded tutorials.
A greedy that steers the beam toward the next unlit sensor beat rooms 1-10 almost always; after the redesign it is at most 20% on rooms 6-22 at 300 s and 0 on 16-22.
The status line now counts the animated lit sensors, Infinity progress clamps to 22, dead fields and parameters were removed, room data is deep-frozen and moved to its own module.

openNotes: Rooms 1-5 are tutorials and are brute-forceable in seconds; the step from 2 turns (room 5) to 4 turns (room 6) is steep.
Undo refunds turns; budgets still hold because a random walk with undo rarely reaches the single solved setting (room 9 is 10 of 40 at 300 s, exactly the bar, and is not a budget room).
The main module is 957 lines, over the 800-line soft ceiling, plus 279 lines of room data.
